note: Batches are scheduling, not pre-registration. What the protocol measures lives in eval-suite-v1.json; this only says how it is divided across jobs. The scoring batches must together cover that set exactly, or running all of them would still not produce the protocol's macro.

batches.name: prepare
batches.why: No GPU. Resolves every pin, materializes every dataset and writes MMMU-Pro's 1730 images, so a bad pin or a gated dataset fails before an allocation rather than four hours into one. MMMU-Pro has never run, and this is the part of that risk which can be retired for free.

batches.name: short-context
batches.why: Everything that tolerates forty or more requests in flight. Kept together because lanes fill each other's tails: GPQA averaged 37 of 192 streams busy and multimodal spent 485 of 502 seconds on a single item, so splitting these pays each tail separately and adds a server load per split.

batches.name: long-context
batches.why: RULER alone. One 128k sequence holds roughly 8.5 GB of KV, so it wants about a dozen requests in flight per replica where the others take forty. Sharing a server means one starves the other, and it would do so to one arm at a time, which is exactly the asymmetry a paired delta cannot absorb.
